items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: I was looking at an old record from around the mid-1960s, with you and Cannonball and another couple of things with Milt Jackson

ctx.x: That’s great. Nicely done. I was looking at an old record from around the mid-1960s, with you and Cannonball and another couple of things with Milt Jackson, and in it you had said something about selling newspapers as a young boy and hearing music from the church and it made an impression on you. Can you tell me about how that felt back at that time?

Well I grew up in a house where everybody went to church on Sunday. My mother cleaned house every Sunday morning. If you came in at eight ten, at eight thirty you left for church. Drunk, sober or whatever, you left. And it was a sort of high-falootin’ for those days, black church and when the music started getting a little bit good if the people started moving a little bit they would say oh no, no, no, no, we don’t want to sound like those heathens you know.
